name: tox-antitargets
description: Antitarget (off-target) protein affinity vs rodent acute toxicity: the server to use for 'Is there a relationship between antitarget affinity and acute toxicity in mice?', 'Which molecular initiating events (MIE, AOP) correlate with acute toxicity?', 'If a strong affinity-LD50 correlation is observed, does that prove a mechanism?', and 'is the correlation real or a logP confounder?' - «Есть ли зависимость между аффинностями к антитаргетам и острой токсичностью мышей?», «Какие молекулярно-инициирующие события могут коррелировать с острой токсичностью?», «Если наблюдается сильная корреляция между аффинностью и LD50, доказывает ли это наличие механизма?». It reproduces Nikitin et al. 2025 (Pharmaceutics 17, 1573, 'Linking Antitargets to Rodent Acute Toxicity') from a public dataset of 12,654 small molecules with mouse intravenous LD50/pLD50 and AutoDock Vina docking scores against the 44-protein Bowes safety pharmacology panel (hERG/KCNH2, AVPR1A, CACNA1C, KCNQ1, EDNRA, acetylcholinesterase, dopamine D2, cannabinoid CB1/CB2, muscarinic, adrenergic, opioid receptors, ion channels). Each question is answered by a SET of tools, chained via metadata.next_tools: dataset scope, ranking of antitargets by the toxicity of their strong-binder subset, Mann-Whitney binder-vs-non-binder pLD50 test (the categorical evidence), per-protein Spearman docking-pLD50 correlation with an inline categorical cross-check, per-chemical-cluster correlation heatmaps, inverse docking / target fishing for a molecule given by SMILES or name (soman, anisodamine, butaperazine, cannabinoids) to test whether a known target is among the strongest binders, and a logP hidden-variable confounder analysis. Also covers hERG / cardiotoxicity ASSOCIATION with antitarget binding, safety pharmacology, mechanism-of-action elucidation, NIH and Brenk medicinal-chemistry filtering, Butina chemical clustering, physicochemical property profiling and chemical-space t-SNE. SCOPE AND LIMITS: drug-like small molecules that are already in the 12,654-compound dataset, with a single administration route (mouse intravenous). This server does NOT predict LD50 or any toxicity endpoint for a new molecule and has no predictive tox model - for LD50 / hepatotoxicity / DILI / cardiotoxicity / carcinogenicity PREDICTION of an arbitrary or plant-derived molecule use the heracleum-tox server (`predict_ld50`, `predict_general_toxicity`, `predict_molecule_profile`). It also does not cover plant extracts, phytotoxins, furanocoumarins, routes of administration other than IV, or pesticidal activity (see cannabis-biopesticide).
